Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Exam mechanics are HEDGED: Montana's own manual (both the Montana-specific front matter, pages MT-1 through MT-8, and the AAMVA base content) never discloses a specific number of items per knowledge test or an explicit passing-score percentage anywhere in the fetched text -- confirmed by exhaustive keyword search for 'questions', 'percent', '80%', and similar terms, which surfaced only generic references to 'the written test includes questions on...' with no item count or score threshold. The federally standardized minimum passing score of 80% under 49 CFR 383.135(a) applies regardless. Third-party CDL test-prep aggregators (not used as a source for any question content, only cited here as corroboration since Montana's own manual is silent) converge on a General Knowledge test of 50 questions with 40 correct (80%) needed to pass, consistent with the AAMVA base-manual convention used by several other states in this project. Montana's Driving Demonstration (skills test) consists of three segments taken in order -- pre-trip vehicle inspection, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test (four exercises: Forward Stop, Straight Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, Reverse Offset Backing), and an On-Road Driving test -- each must be passed before advancing to the next, and failing a step requires rescheduling at least 1 day later (7 days for a failed road test). A Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) must be held at least 14 calendar days before the driving demonstration (test allowed on the 15th day) and is valid for one year. Montana's three CDL vehicle classes are A (Combination Vehicle, GCWR 26,001+ lbs with a towed unit GVWR over 10,000 lbs), B (Heavy Straight Vehicle, GVWR 26,001+ lbs, note: a semi-tractor cannot be used/tested as a Class B vehicle), and C (Small Vehicle meeting neither A nor B, but designed for 16+ passengers including driver or requiring hazmat placarding); Class D is the non-commercial license. Montana's CDL endorsements are H (Hazardous Materials), N (Tank), P (Passenger), T (Double/Triple Trailer), X (combined Tank/Hazmat), and S (School Bus) -- like several other states in this project, Montana does not use a separate charter-bus 'C' endorsement. Only Passenger (P), School Bus (S), and Tank (N) endorsements may be added to a CLP. Age requirements: 18 for Intrastate, 21 for Interstate. A Hazardous Materials endorsement requires a TSA Security Threat Assessment (fingerprint-based background check). Mandatory FMCSA Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT), effective November 13, 2023, is required before a first-time Class A or B license, a Class B-to-A upgrade, or a first-time School Bus/Passenger/Hazardous Materials endorsement. Major-offense CDL suspensions run 1 year (first offense; 3 years if transporting placarded hazmat) to life (second offense, or any offense involving a CMV used for human trafficking or a controlled-substance felony); serious traffic violations carry 60-day (2 violations/3 years) to 120-day (3 violations/3 years) suspensions; railroad grade crossing violations run 60 days (1st) to 120 days (2nd) to 1 year (3rd+) within a three-year period. A military CDL test waiver and a restricted seasonal CDL (farm-related service industries, valid March 15-September 10 within a 150-mile radius) are both available. Content-depth rationale: Montana uses the same AAMVA-authored 'Modernized Testing System' base manual (Version: July 2017) as several other recently built CDL-track states in this project (e.g. Kentucky, Louisiana, Missouri, Massachusetts), organized into the same 13 core sections -- Section 1 Introduction, Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split here into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering vehicle inspection through mountain driving [subsections 2.1-2.16], 03_driving_safely_b covering driving emergencies through hazardous materials rules for all commercial drivers [subsections 2.17-2.23]), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split into two buckets: 10_hazmat_a covering intent/hazard classes/shipping papers/placarding/loading through subsection 9.4, 11_hazmat_b covering bulk packaging marking through the glossary, subsections 9.5-9.8), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection, Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test and Section 13 On-Road Driving (combined into one bucket), plus Montana-specific administrative detail (definitions, licensing requirements, classifications, endorsements/restrictions, fees, medical/self-certification, disqualifications, proof of identity/residence documents) layered into the licensing bucket from the manual's Montana-specific front matter (pages MT-1 through MT-8). Some sections (Cargo, Doubles/Triples, Tank Vehicles) are naturally short in this manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Montana manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers -- all numeric specifications (air brake PSI thresholds, tire tread depth minimums, weight/capacity figures, suspension timeframes) were verified against the actual Montana text read by the drafting process, not assumed from other states' manuals even where those states share the same AAMVA base document.
